answer: Grading panels are drawn from a 12-epoch rotated pool using commit-reveal randomness, so a sybil cluster cannot predict which relic-grade jurors it must corrupt. Each planted grader raises the chance of being audited by a 0.1 honeypot rate, and the expected fine makes the per-identity cost of subversion grow faster than the identities. The system verifies by re-examining pulse-settled grades with seeded honeypots and slashing diverging trellis graders.
